findings.title: Unreadable B2 lifecycle rules slip past the cutover's check step
findings.description: `CHECK_ALLOWED = (r"^(\S+|PENDING RESTART) 17/tick ", ...)` allows *any* `MISSING 17/tick …` line, including `MISSING 17/tick lifecycle-read (…)` — which `setup-backup.sh` deliberately tallies as a failure (`deploy/setup-backup.sh` step 3, `report "MISSING $C lifecycle-read …"`). `step_check` (lines 87–96) verifies only that a `SUMMARY` was printed and that `setup_not_ok` is empty; it never checks the exit code, so a run where rclone/B2 credentials are unreadable passes step 2 and is only caught later (step 4 `apply` or step 12 `production` do reject it via `APPLY_ALLOWED` and the `returncode == 0` require). That matches the stated intent ("17/tick not yet set up" is expected at check time) and is not data-endangering, but the asymmetry is worth a comment or an explicit exclusion of `lifecycle-read` from `CHECK_ALLOWED`.

findings.title: `strip_new_args` hardcodes the main cluster's replication host
findings.description: `strip_new_args` removes `" --replication-host 127.0.0.1"` as a literal, duplicating the value that `deploy/backup-clusters.conf` row `17/main` declares in its `replication_host` column. If that column is ever edited, the strip silently stops matching and `step_apply` would report a spurious production-lines change (fail-safe direction, but a confusing one). The function is only ever applied to 17/main lines so the hardcoded host is correct today; threading the value out of `cluster(TABLE_PATH, MAIN).replication_host` would remove the duplication.

findings.title: `main()` indexes the first production line without an empty guard
findings.description: `user = production_lines(CRON_FILE.read_text())[0].split()[5]` raises an unexplained `IndexError` if `/etc/cron.d/manta-trading-backup` is empty or unreadable as this user before the run — the script's own convention is explicit `sys.exit` messages (as the following `getpass` and bucket checks do). An empty-check with `sys.exit("no production job lines in …")` would match the rest of `main()`.

findings.title: Render, table parsing, and parity are sound
findings.description: Verified against the files: `render_cron.sh` substitutes cluster blocks in table order, quotes every replacement (the `2>&1` patsub hazard is documented and covered by `test_ampersand_survives_substitution`), and rejects missing `--pgdata` and malformed tables before emitting stdout. The `##`-comment stripping (`grep -v '^##'`) is covered by `test_block_order`. The Python and bash parsers of `backup-clusters.conf` agree on 15 fields, `-` optionality, url-key and `/data/` root validation. `b2_lifecycle.sh` is strictly read-only and documents exactly why (rclone v1.75.0 would replace every bucket rule) — an exemplary safety note — and `test_never_sets_a_rule` mechanically proves it only ever calls `backend lifecycle`. `setup-backup.sh` parses the table before any step, sources each data dir from `pg_lsclusters` rather than deriving it, and prefixes per-cluster items so `test_setup_backup.py` can distinguish host from cluster items.

findings.title: Test coverage follows the project's fixture-realism rules
findings.description: The tests exercise the real render (running `render_cron.sh` against the checked-in table), the real pre-227 fixture, and the actual format production emits (per the project's parser-testing rule), with the host calls (`psql`, `shell`, `run`, `setup_backup`) patched at module level. Step-level behavior (arm-only-on-success, restart-only-tick, lock re-check before restart, WAL wait bound) each has a dedicated test, and `test_setup_backup.py` adds rehearse-root, malformed-table, and lifecycle-rule matrix coverage. No gaps found on the critical paths.

structured_findings.summary: Unreadable B2 lifecycle rules slip past the cutover's check step
`strip_new_args` hardcodes the main cluster's replication host
`main()` indexes the first production line without an empty guard
Render, table parsing, and parity are sound
Test coverage follows the project's fixture-realism rules
